The element is the article's lead photo, an aerial view of an FPSO oil production ship at sea with a helideck, stylised by a filter. Its alt is exactly the visible caption below it, which is a

, not a figcaption: "Petrobras: dados de produção do 3º tri bateram recorde (MAURO PIMENTEL/AFP/Getty Images)". claimTrue is yes. The alt states a news fact, that production data broke a record, and gives a photo credit. The image shows neither data nor a record. elementFails is yes. The alt gives none of what the photo conveys: no ship, no platform, nothing about the scene. A screen reader user hears the caption twice and never learns what is pictured. That falls short of G94 (an alternative presenting the same information as the image). The photo is the editorial lead image, not decoration. Read in good faith, the claim names this defect (the rubric's own example). captureDiffers is no: the live HTML has the same image src, the same alt and the same caption, and the screenshot is styled.

It is <input id=email type=email name=email> with no autocomplete attribute. claimTrue is yes: no autocomplete in the capture, and the snapshot records Chrome's form issue FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError on this field, so 'Chromium's own form check flags it' holds. elementFails is yes. The field collects the user's own email address, which is an Input Purpose ('email') under 1.3.5. type=email gives the data format but not that this is the user's own address. Without autocomplete="email" (H98), the purpose is not programmatically determined. captureDiffers is no: the live server HTML has the same input with no autocomplete, and the screenshot shows the field rendered as captured.

That satisfies 1.1.1, and the image is exposed with its alt (CDP: image, nameFrom alt). The alt repeats the headline link next to it, which is redundant but no 1.1.1 failure. The link around it has no name in Chrome because of the <figure> wrapper. That is a 4.1.2 failure of the link, reported separately, not a fault of this image's alternative. elementFails is no. captureDiffers is no: the live HTML has the same card, image and alt. Rampa was right to report nothing.
